Judge Dismisses Trump’s $10 B Defamation Suit Against Wall Street Journal Over Epstein Letter

03 Nov 2026, 02:17 AM IST · GlobeWire Daily World Desk · Source: www.aljazeera.com

Image: Al Jazeera Staff · Photo source · Resized and letterboxed to 16:9; no AI generation

Key takeaways Summary A U.S. federal judge has permanently thrown out former President Donald Trump’s multibillion‑dollar defamation lawsuit against media mogul Rupert Murdoch and The Wall Street Journal (WSJ). The ruling, issued by U.S. District Judge Darrin Gayles in Miami, found

Summary

A U.S. federal judge has permanently thrown out former President Donald Trump’s multibillion‑dollar defamation lawsuit against media mogul Rupert Murdoch and The Wall Street Journal (WSJ). The ruling, issued by U.S. District Judge Darrin Gayles in Miami, found that Trump failed to meet the legal standard of “actual malice” required to prove defamation.

Legal Findings

  • Standard not met: Under U.S. defamation law, a plaintiff must show the defendant published a false statement knowing it was false or with reckless disregard for the truth. Judge Gayles said Trump’s amended complaint was vague, conclusory and did not plead actual malice.
  • Dismissal with prejudice: The case was dismissed “with prejudice,” meaning Trump cannot re‑file the same claim.
  • Judge’s comment: Gayles described the lawsuit as “grasping at straws” and suggested Trump’s lawyers tried to “manufacture flaws” in the WSJ investigation.

Background of the WSJ Report

  • July 17 2025 article: The WSJ published an exclusive that linked Trump to a sexually suggestive birthday note allegedly written for Jeffrey Epstein’s 50th birthday in 2003.
  • Letter details: The note reportedly featured typed text surrounded by a hand‑drawn outline of a curvaceous woman, with Trump’s signature at the bottom.
  • Source of the letter: The correspondence was said to have been collected by Ghislaine Maxwell, now serving a 20‑year sentence for her role in Epstein’s sex‑trafficking network.
  • House Oversight release: A copy of the birthday letter was later made public by the House Oversight Committee.

Trump’s Response

  • Denial: Trump has consistently denied authoring the note, the signature, or the artwork.
  • Defamation claim: Filed on July 18 2025 in federal court in Miami, the lawsuit alleged the WSJ and its reporters knowingly and recklessly published false, defamatory statements, causing “overwhelming financial and reputational harm.”
  • Re‑filing: After an initial dismissal in April, Trump amended the complaint in May, arguing the newspaper was reckless in verifying the letter’s provenance.

Practical Implications

  • Financial impact: The dismissal removes the possibility of a $10 billion judgment against the WSJ, preserving the newspaper’s financial stability.
  • Precedent: The decision reinforces the high bar for public‑figure defamation suits, especially the requirement to prove actual malice.
  • Ongoing litigation: Trump still faces separate defamation cases against other outlets such as the BBC and The New York Times.

How to Verify the Information

  • Court documents: The full opinion by Judge Darrin Gayles is publicly available through the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Florida’s PACER system.
  • WSJ article: The original July 2025 WSJ piece can be accessed on the newspaper’s website or through reputable news archives.
  • House Oversight release: The letter copy released by the House Oversight Committee is posted on the committee’s official website.
  • Official statements: Both Trump’s legal team and the WSJ have issued press releases that can be cross‑checked for consistency.
